details.label: Summary
details.text: The risk of severe wind gusts and very large hail continues across parts of the Nebraska Panhandle this evening. The severe risk may spread south of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 612 into northeastern Colorado, and a downstream watch issuance is possible

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A robust right-moving supercell has recently intensified in the NE Panhandle as it encounters a maximum in surface-based buoyancy, driven by a plume of upper 60s dewpoints and steep deep-layer lapse rates. Around 50-60 kt of effective shear will continue to support this storm with southward extent, posing a risk of very large hail (recent reports of baseball-sized hail) and severe wind gusts. Given the warm/moist air mass downstream into northeast CO, and the potential for storm mergers amid a gradually strengthening nocturnal LLJ, an organized cluster could persist/spread south of the watch, and trends are being monitored for a downstream watch

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK TORNADO INTENSITY...UP TO 90 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...65-80 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...2.00-3.50 IN

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: A threat for locally damaging wind may continue through dusk

details.label: Summary
details.text: A threat for locally damaging wind may continue through dusk

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Vigorous convection is spreading south-southwestward across southern LA this evening. Deep-layer flow/shear is weak, but very rich moisture (with 0-1 km mean mixing ratios of 20+ g/kg and PW well above 2 inches) and large MLCAPE of 3000-5000 J/kg (as observed on the LCH sounding) will continue to support a threat of at least localized wind damage, until storms weaken or move offshore later this evening. Some severe threat will spread south of ongoing watches, but the limited spatiotemporal extent of the remaining threat should preclude additional watch issuance

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Thunderstorms will pose a risk of severe wind gusts and large hail during the next couple hours

details.label: Summary
details.text: Thunderstorms will pose a risk of severe wind gusts and large hail during the next couple hours

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Several thunderstorms have recently intensified along a subtle surface boundary and in a zone of enhanced low-level convergence near a surface low in east-central CO. This activity is evolving along the eastern periphery of a large-scale ridge, where around 40 kt of effective shear is promoting convective organization (including supercells). These storms should continue tracking slowly southward along a buoyancy gradient, where a deeply mixed PBL will promote severe wind gusts over the next couple hours. Isolated instances of large hail will also be possible with the longer-lived supercell structures

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...55-70 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...1.00-1.75 IN
